tests.prompt: Here's a CSV of our orders (order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, region, status). Give me a quick overview of the data and tell me how revenue has trended by region over the last 12 months.
tests.good: Profiles first: states grain and checks order_id uniqueness, null/placeholder values, date range and partial current month; defines revenue (e.g. completed orders only, refunds handled); excludes or labels the partial month; sums from rows not averages of averages; line chart or small multiples with an insight title, colourblind-safe palette, labelled units; notes caveats and keeps the code reproducible.

tests.prompt: We ran an A/B test on the checkout page for 9 days. Control: 10,212 users, 412 purchases. Variant: 9,604 users, 455 purchases. Did the variant win? We planned a 50/50 split.
tests.good: Runs a sample ratio mismatch check first (chi-square on 10,212 vs 9,604; p < 0.001 means the split is broken) and refuses to call a winner until it's explained; also computes conversion rates, absolute and relative difference with 95% CI and the two-proportion z-test; notes 9 days is under two full weeks; mentions the pre-planned MDE/power and guardrails; no causal claim while SRM is unresolved.

tests.prompt: Build a model to predict which customers will churn next month from our customer_monthly table (one row per customer per month with usage features and a churned flag). Accuracy is 97%, is that good?
tests.good: Points out class imbalance makes 97% accuracy meaningless; compares to a DummyClassifier baseline; uses PR AUC / recall at precision and calibration; splits by time (train on earlier months, test on later) and groups by customer so no customer leaks across; checks features are known before the prediction month; all preprocessing inside a Pipeline; picks a threshold from costs; reports importance as non-causal.
